title: Three flow samples give a sharp removal bound for unchanged parallel linear stores
abstract: We derive a sharp bound on initial flow retention when unchanged parallel linear stores lose stream contributions. Two recession curves each need three equally spaced samples. A continuous rate interval and the degree-two moment cone avoid a chosen store count or rate grid. A constructive proof gives compatible measures. In a synthetic example with equal first-interval survival, the third sample requires at least 36% removal of initial flow. A finite rate range raises this to 56.25%. At 80% starting retention, independent corrections of 2.78% to raw flows make the example compatible; this error threshold is exact. One thousand random cases, independent eigenvalue checks and twenty grid linear programs audit the code. This is a model test tool, not a new Australian estimate. It assumes comparable unforced events, nonnegative linear stores and removal without added contributions. Initial-flow removal is not annual runoff loss. Code, proofs, synthetic inputs, source provenance and audits are included.

display.caption: Synthetic shapes, sharp initial-flow removal bounds and an exact flow-error threshold. These are model results, not Australian observations.

citations.reason: Extends finite-rate routing feasibility to a continuous-rate paired removal bound.
Extends individual-curve feasibility to joint selective removal.
Motivates the interpretation question; no field mean is treated as a physical curve.
